body.statement: When \(k=1\), the criterion reduces to \(\Phi_1(d)=1+\sum_{i=1}^p r(d_i)\), and the optimizer reduces to the uniform limited-supply dosage in the additive PFED setting. When \(L\ge p/2\), it further reduces to half dosage with \(\Phi^\star=1+p\).
body.justification: This is the required sanity reduction to the known additive and unconstrained designs.
body.gap: The reduction is known from ShyamalZhangUhler2025; it is included as a fidelity check rather than a novelty claim.
body.consumer: Readers can verify that the all-order theorem preserves the established additive benchmark.
body.proof_tex:
When \(k=1\), the retained family consists only of the empty set and the \(p\) singletons. The trace identity immediately becomes
\[
 \Phi_1(d)=1+\sum_{i=1}^p r(d_i).
\]
The uniform-optimum theorem gives the unique optimizer \(d_i=u=\min\{L/p,1/2\}\), which is the uniform limited-supply dosage in the additive product-Bernoulli design. If \(L\ge p/2\), then \(u=1/2\) and \(r(1/2)=1\), so
\[
 \Phi^\star=1+p.
\]
